methodology.title: Methodology — how the AI Leaderboard is computed
methodology.description: How we match model names across leaderboards, compute percentiles and disagreement flags, and validate every data update.
methodology.intro: Every number on this site is reproduced from a public source. We never average scores from different scales; we compare positions.
methodology.matchingP: Each source names models differently. A hand-maintained alias table maps every source name to one canonical model. Matching is exact or ignores only case, spaces and punctuation. Similar-looking names are queued for human review and are never applied automatically; unmatched rows are stored but not published.
methodology.variantsP: Same weights means the same model. Thinking modes, style control, quantization or provider are variants of that model; a model's rank on a board uses its best variant. Different weights (for example DeepSeek R1 vs. V3) are different models.
methodology.percentileP: Within each published snapshot we compute a percentile among matched models: (N − rank + 1) / N × 100, so 100 is first place. Percentiles make boards of different sizes and scales comparable; raw Elo and accuracy are never averaged together.
methodology.disagreementP: For each category (coding, math…) we look at every board that measures it. If a model's percentile differs by {threshold} points or more between two of them, it gets a disagreement flag, and the size of the gap ranks the "biggest disagreements". Comparing only within a category avoids false alarms like "math vs. Chinese".
methodology.validationP: Every update is checked before publishing. Critical problems — a row count drop of more than 30%, a schema change, all scores missing or out of range — reject that batch and keep the last good data online. Softer warnings (low match rate, new categories, big Top-10 changes) are logged for review.
methodology.sourcesP: Rankings come from LMArena and Epoch AI. OpenRouter supplies prices and context length only. Sources whose redistribution terms are not confirmed are kept switched off.
methodology.historyP: LMArena publishes a dated history, so trends go back to the first available snapshot. Trend lines break where a source changes its question set or method.
